back2basics.text: Election tribunals are quasi-judicial bodies that hear disputes related to electoral rolls, such as inclusion or deletion of voter names. Electoral rolls are official lists of eligible voters in a constituency, and their accuracy is crucial for fair elections. The Special Intensive Revision (SIR) is a process to update and verify these rolls before elections. Judicial oversight ensures disputes are resolved promptly to uphold electoral integrity.

back2basics.text: Prorogation is the formal ending of a parliamentary session by the President on the advice of the Council of Ministers. It differs from adjournment, which is a temporary suspension of sitting. Prorogation clears the agenda of the current session and is necessary before a new session can be summoned. The Constitution requires at least two sessions annually, with no more than six months between sessions.

2026-11-23-pm-2ed9527c05.deck: The Constitution mandates that the President, on the Council of Ministers' advice, summons and prorogues Parliament sessions, ensuring no more than six months between sessions. body.label: Focus on prevention
body.text: India is moving from post-disaster relief to anticipating risks, strengthening early warning systems, and preventing loss of lives and infrastructure in landslide-prone areas.

body.label: Landslide mapping and data
body.text: National landslide susceptibility mapping covers approximately 4.3 lakh sq km, and an inventory of nearly 91,000 historical landslides has been compiled.

body.label: Vaccination and indigenous innovation
body.text: Over 50 lakh adolescent girls have been vaccinated against HPV to prevent cervical cancer, reflecting progress in indigenous vaccine development.

body.label: Precision medicine and rare diseases
body.text: Research includes biomarkers for gestational diabetes and expanding diagnosis and treatment coverage for rare genetic diseases to improve affordability and access.

body.label: Advances in therapies
body.text: Indian researchers are developing genetic therapies, new antibiotics, and gene therapy for haemophilia, indicating growing indigenous medical research capabilities.

body.label: Healthcare infrastructure
body.text: Expansion of dialysis facilities in district hospitals and research on early kidney disease detection improve treatment access and disease management.

body.label: Collaboration and awareness

back2basics.text: The anti-defection law aims to prevent elected legislators from switching parties after elections, which can destabilize governments. It provides grounds for disqualification of members who defect from their party. The law's adjudication is typically handled by the Speaker or Chairman of the legislature, who decides on disqualification petitions. However, concerns about misuse and delays have led to calls for reforms.

2026-11-23-pm-822a994f87.deck: The Supreme Court on November 23, 2026, sought responses from the Centre, Election Commission of India, Law Commission, and relevant ministries on a PIL demanding reforms in the anti-defection law. These reforms aim to address misuse of resignations by legislators to evade disqualification and manipulate government stability, a critical issue for governance and legislative ethics.

body.label: Misuse of resignations
body.text: The PIL highlights that elected representatives misuse resignations to avoid disqualification proceedings under the Tenth Schedule and influence government survival.

body.label: Strategic resignations
body.text: Legislators facing or anticipating disqualification often resign strategically before the Speaker or Chairman can decide on their cases, enabling political realignments and altering assembly strength.

body.label: Need for adjudication reforms
body.text: The PIL seeks time-bound, reasoned, and transparent adjudication of resignations and disqualification proceedings, and institutional review of the Speaker-centred adjudicatory mechanism.

body.label: Majority testing in hung assemblies
body.text: It demands reaffirmation that government majority in a hung assembly must be tested on the floor of the House after members are sworn in, not through extra-parliamentary letters or demonstrations.

body.label: Purpose of VRR auction
body.text: The RBI conducts Variable Rate Repo auctions to manage short-term liquidity in the banking system by borrowing excess cash from banks at variable interest rates.

body.label: Details of the November 23, 2026 auction
body.text: On November 23, 2026, RBI conducted a 4-day VRR auction with a notified amount of ₹50,000 crore, receiving bids worth ₹1,51,982 crore and allotting ₹50,005 crore at a cut-off rate of 5.62%.

body.label: Auction mechanics
body.text: The auction tenor was 4 days, with the window open from 10:30 AM to 11:00 AM, and the amount borrowed was reversed on November 25, 2026.

body.label: Conference purpose
body.text: MoSPI organised a Data Users Conference on November 23, 2026, to familiarise users with the methodological changes, data sources, and improvements in the revised GDP, CPI, and IIP series.

body.label: GDP revisions
body.text: The new GDP series with base year 2022-23 includes double deflation for manufacturing, use of administrative data like MCA-21 filings, and improved measurement of unincorporated sectors and private consumption.

body.label: CPI revisions
body.text: The CPI series rebased to 2024=100 uses updated consumption baskets from the 2023-24 Household Consumption Expenditure Survey, expanded coverage, COICOP 2018 classification, and incorporates administrative and e-commerce data.

body.label: IIP revisions
body.text: The IIP series rebased to 2022-23 broadens sector coverage by adding water supply, sewerage, waste management, and gas supply sectors, revises weights using National Accounts and ASI data, and uses Output PPI for deflation.

sections.heading: What are the key changes in the new GDP, CPI, and IIP data series?

body.label: Improved data quality
body.text: The revisions incorporate new data sources and methodologies that better reflect structural changes in the economy, consumption patterns, and production processes.

body.label: Policy implications
body.text: More accurate GDP, CPI, and IIP estimates help the RBI and policymakers make informed decisions on inflation targeting, growth assessment, and liquidity management.

body.label: RBI's role
body.text: RBI, as a committed user and knowledge partner, emphasises stable estimates with smaller revisions and continued dialogue with MoSPI for clarity and predictability.

sections.heading: Why do these updates matter for monetary policy and economic analysis?

mcq.stem:
Consider the following statements about the India-Nepal Ayodhya-Janakpur rail link and development package:
1. The Sarayu-Kamala Express covers 604 kilometres and operates once a week.
2. India's development assistance to Nepal includes a ₹15,000 crore package with a grant component and a Line of Credit for energy projects.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcq.trap: Statement 1 is correct about the rail link; Statement 2 is correct about the development package. A trap would be confusing the total package amount or the frequency of the train.

body.label: Rail service details
body.text: The Sarayu-Kamala Express connects Ayodhya in India to Janakpur in Nepal, covering 604 kilometres in about 19 hours without requiring passengers to change trains.

body.label: Train configuration
body.text: The train uses modern 17-coach LHB rakes including eight air-conditioned coaches, seven sleeper-class coaches, and coaches for luggage and disabled-friendly facilities.

body.label: Frequency and route
body.text: It operates once a week, departing Ayodhya every Monday evening and returning from Janakpur every Saturday afternoon, passing through key stations like Gorakhpur, Raxaul, and Jaynagar.

body.label: Cultural significance
body.text: Ayodhya and Janakpur are important religious sites linked to Lord Ram and Goddess Sita respectively, and the rail link supports the Ramayana Circuit and religious tourism.

sections.heading: What are the key features of the Ayodhya-Janakpur rail link?

body.label: Package components
body.text: India announced development assistance of ₹15,000 crore comprising ₹3,500 crore in grant assistance for post-disaster reconstruction and infrastructure, and ₹11,500 crore as a Rupee-denominated Line of Credit for energy sector projects.

body.label: Project focus
body.text: The assistance targets reconstruction after the August 2026 floods, new infrastructure projects, hydropower development including the Lower Arun Hydro-Electric Project, and capacity building.

body.label: Additional cooperation
body.text: India will support Nepal in sectors like education, agriculture, health, digital connectivity, petroleum supply infrastructure, and sports development.

sections.heading: What does India's ₹15,000 crore development package for Nepal include?

body.label: Strengthening cultural ties
body.text: The rail link and joint initiatives reinforce centuries-old cultural, religious, and people-to-people connections symbolized by shared reverence for Lord Ram and Goddess Sita.

body.label: Improving connectivity
body.text: New railway lines, motorable bridges, Integrated Check Posts, and petroleum pipelines improve trade, transit, and mobility between the two countries.

body.label: Joint Vision Document
body.text: The leaders adopted a Joint Vision for 'Viksit Bharat and Samunnat Nepal' outlining cooperation in economic partnership, connectivity, energy, climate resilience, technology, education, and tourism.

body.label: Regional development
body.text: Enhanced connectivity and infrastructure projects aim to boost Nepal’s economic growth, disaster resilience, and integration with India’s markets and supply chains.

sections.heading: How does this cooperation enhance India-Nepal relations?

body.label: Railway projects
body.text: Survey for the Raxaul-Kathmandu electrified broad-gauge railway line is finalized, with plans to develop the East-West Railway in Nepal and complete Jayanagar-Bardibas and Jogbani-Biratnagar lines.

body.label: Border infrastructure
body.text: New Integrated Check Posts at Banbasa and Dodhara Chandani are being developed, alongside operational ICPs at Bhairahawa, Sunauli, and others.

body.label: Petroleum pipelines
body.text: Phase II of the Motihari-Amlekhgunj Pipeline was inaugurated, and a petroleum terminal at Jhapa is planned, with future gas pipeline cooperation under discussion.

body.label: Bridges and roads
body.text: A new motorable bridge between Dharchula (India) and Darchula (Nepal) was inaugurated to improve direct connectivity in western Nepal.

sections.heading: What are the future connectivity and infrastructure plans?
